hero.heading:
Saint Maron Church
Maronite Catholic
hero.eyebrow: Est. 1892 · Eparchy of Saint Maron of Brooklyn
hero.lede: One of the first Maronite parishes in North America, Saint Maron Church has faithfully served the faithful in South Philadelphia since 1892. For generations, our parish has been a home of prayer, worship, and communion, preserving and sharing the rich spiritual heritage of the Maronite Catholic Church.

parish.heading: Saint Maron Maronite Catholic Church
parish.caption: Original Church Building (1901-1968)
parish.story:
Founded by Lebanese immigrants at the close of the nineteenth century, Saint Maron has been a spiritual home for generations of families in South Philadelphia. We worship in the ancient Maronite tradition — one of the Eastern Catholic Churches in full communion with Rome — with a liturgy whose roots reach back to the earliest Christian communities of Antioch.

Whether your family has been here for a hundred years or you are stepping inside for the first time, you belong here.

sections.heading: Christmas Giving Tree
sections.text:
“For I was hungry and you gave me food, I was thirsty and you gave me drink.” (Matthew 25:35)

 Thank you to everyone who generously donated to our annual Thanksgiving Food Drive. Your kindness and generosity help us care for our brothers and sisters in need by giving them the opportunity to gather around the Thanksgiving table and share a meal filled with love, fellowship, and gratitude.

As our Thanksgiving Food Drive comes to an end, we joyfully continue another beautiful parish tradition: our Christmas Giving Tree!

What a beautiful opportunity to express our love for the Lord by remembering others, especially those who may be experiencing difficult times. Through the simple act of giving a gift, we share the joy, hope, and love of Christ with our brothers and sisters in need. We invite everyone to take part in this special tradition and help make Christmas brighter for those in our community.

May our generosity be a reflection of God's love, and may we remember that the greatest gift of Christmas is Jesus Himself.

May God bless you for your continued kindness and generosity!
